attribution.note: Zitron's own question to Acemoglu in his published interview. He states it in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'it feels' and 'seems' hedges, the 'every report' scope and the word 'people'. It reports his impression of how the coverage reads.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats this as a doubly hedged impression with no defined set of reports and no measure. Turning it into a literal universal claim would overstate what he said.

evidence.note: Goldman Sachs, June 2024. Shows skeptical coverage existed before the interview, but cannot test a subjective impression.
Sequoia, June 2024. Mixes skepticism with optimism about future value. Bears on the tenor of reporting, not on the hedged impression.

reviews.rationale: The statement is an explicitly hedged impression ('it feels', 'seems') about reports in general, with no set of reports, no beneficiary and no measure of money. Under the policy, hedged language is not scored. The evidence is context only.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his published interview.

semantics.note: 'These companies' refers to the big tech firms discussed just before. The two-part conjunction is kept, as is the unhedged present tense.

contract.note: Reading growth as revenue growth across a big-tech panel in Q1 2024 is fair and ordinary. Its clause barring any score because of the 'unknown' accounting basis is overcautious, since reported revenue is the ordinary basis. Still, the panel and the 'new thing' test are left undefined.

evidence.note: Microsoft's unaudited disclosure: 17% revenue growth in the target quarter, up from 7% a year earlier. Growth sped up at the one named company, against a slowing pattern for that member.
Microsoft's prior-year quarter (7%). It is the comparison point for e1 and falls outside the target period.
Apple revenue fell 4% year over year. That fits weakness at one firm, but with no earlier comparison it does not show slowing, and it says nothing about opportunities.

reviews.rationale: Only two companies are documented. Microsoft sped up and Apple shrank, so no panel-wide pattern is shown, and Meta could not be retrieved. Nothing addresses the second part, that no new growth business or acquisition was available. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own interjection in his published interview. 'It' means generative AI.

semantics.note: A firm, unhedged universal claim ('anything'). 'Really' is an intensifier, not a statement of probability. The proposition matches the words.

contract.note: The plain reading, that genAI completes real tasks without a human doing each one, is ordinary. Using the latest full quarter before publication is reasonable. 'Really' does not plausibly require error-free work.

evidence.note: Intercom disclosure, April 2024: Fin resolved an average of 46% of questions in deployments. This is a vendor figure, but it documents automated task completion in the period.
Intercom, June 2024. Describes Fin generating answers straight to customers, which supports the mechanism behind e1.

Customer forum post, May 2024. It questions how resolutions are counted but also says Fin sometimes answers correctly. Labelling it 'independent measurement' overstates it. A promotional comment from 2026 in the thread is ignored.

reviews.rationale: The claim says genAI automates nothing. During the target quarter, Intercom reports deployed Fin agents resolving customer questions without humans, and a customer's own account confirms some correct automated answers. The resolution rate may be inflated, but some real automation is documented, which defeats 'anything'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his published interview.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'it feels like' hedge. It is unclear who 'they' are: AI companies or the firms adopting AI. The flat claim in the preceding sentence is a separate claim.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats the sentence as a hedged impression that cannot be scored without dropping the hedge.

reviews.rationale: 'It feels like' turns the sentence into a tentative impression, and hedged statements are not scored under the policy. The referent and the standard for 'successfully' are also undefined. The packet has no evidence items.
